Every key in Airflow's core configuration: 25 sections, 334 keys. Set a key in `airflow.cfg`, or with the environment variable `AIRFLOW__<SECTION>__<KEY>` (upper case, double underscores), which wins over the file. Keys marked **sensitive** also accept `AIRFLOW__<SECTION>__<KEY>_CMD` and `_SECRET`; see [Configuration and Tuning](../05_deployment_and_config/01_configuration_and_tuning.md).

Provider sections (`[celery]`, `[kubernetes_executor]`, `[fab]`, `[smtp_provider]` and others) are defined by each provider's `provider.yaml` and are not listed here. Defaults are as written in `config.yml`: `{AIRFLOW_HOME}` is expanded at run time, and an empty default means unset.

## [core]

<a id="core.dags_folder"></a>

### `dags_folder`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `{AIRFLOW_HOME}/dags` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__DAGS_FOLDER` |

The folder where your airflow pipelines live, most likely a
subfolder in a code repository. This path must be absolute.

<a id="core.hostname_callable"></a>

### `hostname_callable`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `airflow.utils.net.getfqdn` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__HOSTNAME_CALLABLE` |

Hostname by providing a path to a callable, which will resolve the hostname.
The format is "package.function".

For example, default value `airflow.utils.net.getfqdn` means that result from patched
version of [socket.getfqdn()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/socket.html#socket.getfqdn),
see related [CPython Issue](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/49254).

No argument should be required in the function specified.
If using IP address as hostname is preferred, use value `airflow.utils.net.get_host_ip_address`

<a id="core.might_contain_dag_callable"></a>

### `might_contain_dag_callable`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `airflow.utils.file.might_contain_dag_via_default_heuristic` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MIGHT_CONTAIN_DAG_CALLABLE` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

A callable to check if a python file has airflow dags defined or not and should
return `True` if it has dags otherwise `False`.
If this is not provided, Airflow uses its own heuristic rules.

The function should have the following signature

```python
def func_name(file_path: str, zip_file: zipfile.ZipFile | None = None) -> bool: ...
```

| | |
| :--- | :--- |

<a id="core.executor"></a>

### `executor`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `LocalExecutor` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTOR` |

The executor class that airflow should use. Choices include
`LocalExecutor`, `CeleryExecutor`,
`KubernetesExecutor` or the full import path to the class when using a custom executor.

<a id="core.mp_start_method"></a>

### `mp_start_method`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MP_START_METHOD` |
| Example | `fork` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

The `multiprocessing` start method used by long-lived components that spawn worker
processes (the scheduler's `LocalExecutor` and the triggerer). Must be
one of the values returned by `multiprocessing.get_all_start_methods()
<https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.get_all_start_methods>`__
on your platform (typically `fork`, `forkserver` or `spawn`). When unset (the
default) the platform default is used.

Python 3.14 changed the Unix default from `fork` to `forkserver`. `forkserver` and
`spawn` children re-import Airflow instead of sharing it copy-on-write, which can sharply
increase the resident memory of the scheduler and triggerer. Set this to `fork` to restore
the pre-3.14 behaviour (note: forking a multi-threaded process is not always safe), or keep
`forkserver` and set `[core] mp_forkserver_preload` to recover most of the sharing.

This can be overridden per component by setting `mp_start_method` in the `[scheduler]`,
`[triggerer]` or `[dag_processor]` section.

<a id="core.mp_forkserver_preload"></a>

### `mp_forkserver_preload`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MP_FORKSERVER_PRELOAD` |
| Example | `airflow,airflow.executors.local_executor` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

Comma-separated list of modules the `forkserver` process should import up front, so that
forked workers inherit them copy-on-write instead of re-importing them. Only used when the
effective `mp_start_method` is `forkserver`. See `multiprocessing.set_forkserver_preload
<https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.set_forkserver_preload>`__.

<a id="core.auth_manager"></a>

### `auth_manager`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `airflow.api_fastapi.auth.managers.simple.simple_auth_manager.SimpleAuthManager` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__AUTH_MANAGER` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

The auth manager class that airflow should use. Full import path to the auth manager class.

<a id="core.simple_auth_manager_users"></a>

### `simple_auth_manager_users`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `admin:admin` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__SIMPLE_AUTH_MANAGER_USERS` |
| Example | `bob:admin,peter:viewer` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The list of users and their associated role in simple auth manager. If the simple auth manager is
used in your environment, this list controls who can access the environment.

List of user-role delimited with a comma. Each user-role is a colon delimited couple of username and
role. Roles are predefined in simple auth managers: viewer, user, op, admin.

You can also associate users to teams by appending the list of teams (separated by "|") as third item
in the user-role definition. Example: `bob:admin:marketing|hr`.
This can only be used if `[core] multi_team` is set to True.

<a id="core.simple_auth_manager_all_admins"></a>

### `simple_auth_manager_all_admins`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__SIMPLE_AUTH_MANAGER_ALL_ADMINS` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Whether to disable authentication and allow everyone as admin in the environment.

<a id="core.simple_auth_manager_passwords_file"></a>

### `simple_auth_manager_passwords_file`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__SIMPLE_AUTH_MANAGER_PASSWORDS_FILE` |
| Example | `/path/to/passwords.json` |

<a id="core.parallelism"></a>

### `parallelism`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `32` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__PARALLELISM` |

This defines the maximum number of task instances that can run concurrently per scheduler in
Airflow, regardless of the worker count. Generally this value, multiplied by the number of
schedulers in your cluster, is the maximum number of task instances with the running
state in the metadata database. The value must be larger or equal 1.

<a id="core.max_active_tasks_per_dag"></a>

### `max_active_tasks_per_dag`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `16` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MAX_ACTIVE_TASKS_PER_DAG` |
| Added in | 2.2.0 |

The maximum number of task instances allowed to run concurrently in each dag run.
This is also configurable per-dag with `max_active_tasks`,
which is defaulted as `[core] max_active_tasks_per_dag`.

An example scenario when this would be useful is when you want to stop a new dag run with an early
start date from stealing all the executor slots in a cluster.

<a id="core.dags_are_paused_at_creation"></a>

### `dags_are_paused_at_creation`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__DAGS_ARE_PAUSED_AT_CREATION` |

Are DAGs paused by default at creation

<a id="core.max_active_runs_per_dag"></a>

### `max_active_runs_per_dag`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `16` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS_PER_DAG` |

The maximum number of active DAG runs per DAG. The scheduler will not create more DAG runs
if it reaches the limit. This is configurable at the DAG level with `max_active_runs`,
which is defaulted as `[core] max_active_runs_per_dag`.

<a id="core.max_consecutive_failed_dag_runs_per_dag"></a>

### `max_consecutive_failed_dag_runs_per_dag`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `0` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILED_DAG_RUNS_PER_DAG` |
| Added in | 2.9.0 |

(experimental) The maximum number of consecutive DAG failures before DAG is automatically paused.
This is also configurable per DAG level with `max_consecutive_failed_dag_runs`,
which is defaulted as `[core] max_consecutive_failed_dag_runs_per_dag`.
If not specified, then the value is considered as 0,
meaning that the dags are never paused out by default.

<a id="core.load_examples"></a>

### `load_examples`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES` |

Whether to load the Dag examples that ship with Airflow. It's good to
get started, but you probably want to set this to `False` in a production
environment

**Note:** 

    If you are using the Official Airflow Docker Image, this value is set to `False` by default
    via the environment variable `AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES`. To enable example Dags when
    using the official image, you must explicitly set `AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES=True` in your
    environment.

### `plugins_folder`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |

| Type | string |

Path to the folder containing Airflow plugins

<a id="core.execute_tasks_new_python_interpreter"></a>

### `execute_tasks_new_python_interpreter`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Should tasks be executed via forking of the parent process

* `False`: Execute via forking of the parent process
* `True`: Spawning a new python process, slower than fork, but means plugin changes picked
  up by tasks straight away

On Airflow 3 this applies to the task process only. When `True` the supervisor starts
the task in a fresh interpreter with `exec` right after forking it, so the task cannot
inherit a lock a supervisor thread held at fork time (which can otherwise hang it at its
first TLS call). The Dag processor, the triggerer and task callbacks are not affected and
keep bare fork. Each task pays an interpreter start plus re-import. The task process reads
the global value; Edge workers, which resolve it per team, already start a fresh interpreter
for the supervisor when it is `True` and start a second one for the task.

<a id="core.allowed_deserialization_classes"></a>

### `allowed_deserialization_classes`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `airflow.*` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__ALLOWED_DESERIALIZATION_CLASSES` |
| Example | `airflow.* my_mod.my_other_mod.TheseClasses*` |
| Added in | 2.5.0 |

Space-separated list of classes that may be imported during deserialization. Items can be glob
expressions. Python built-in classes (like dict) are always allowed.

<a id="core.allowed_deserialization_classes_regexp"></a>

### `allowed_deserialization_classes_regexp`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__ALLOWED_DESERIALIZATION_CLASSES_REGEXP` |
| Added in | 2.8.2 |

Space-separated list of classes that may be imported during deserialization. Items are processed
as regex expressions and matched against the full classname (`re.fullmatch` semantics), so a
pattern such as `airflow\.models\.Variable` does not also admit `airflow.models.VariableXYZ`.
Use `.*` (e.g. `airflow\.models\..*`) to allow a prefix and any suffix. Python built-in
classes (like dict) are always allowed.
This is a secondary option to `[core] allowed_deserialization_classes`.

<a id="core.killed_task_cleanup_time"></a>

### `killed_task_cleanup_time`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `60` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__KILLED_TASK_CLEANUP_TIME` |

When a task is killed forcefully, this is the amount of time in seconds that
it has to cleanup after it is sent a SIGTERM, before it is SIGKILLED.
The task supervisor also waits this long after `execution_timeout` elapses before
it sends SIGTERM to a task process that has not stopped on its own.

<a id="core.dag_run_conf_overrides_params"></a>

### `dag_run_conf_overrides_params`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__DAG_RUN_CONF_OVERRIDES_PARAMS` |

Whether to override params with dag_run.conf. If you pass some key-value pairs
through `airflow dags backfill -c` or
`airflow dags trigger -c`, the key-value pairs will override the existing ones in params.

<a id="core.dag_discovery_safe_mode"></a>

### `dag_discovery_safe_mode`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__DAG_DISCOVERY_SAFE_MODE` |
| Added in | 1.10.3 |

If enabled, Airflow only scans files containing both `DAG` and `airflow` (case-insensitive)
when looking for Dags. Set this to `False` to scan every Python file instead -- required when
your Dags are defined through a wrapper or abstraction whose source does not contain those strings.

This setting is read by the Dag file processor, so it must be configured for that component. In a
separate-process deployment (for example the Helm chart) set it on the `dag-processor` as well as
on anything that runs `airflow dags reserialize`, and restart the component for a change to take
effect. If only some components see `False`, Dags can appear after a manual reserialize and then
be deactivated again on the next processor scan.

As an alternative to scanning every file, set `[core] might_contain_dag_callable` to a custom
heuristic that recognizes your wrapper.

<a id="core.dag_ignore_file_syntax"></a>

### `dag_ignore_file_syntax`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `glob` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__DAG_IGNORE_FILE_SYNTAX` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The pattern syntax used in the
`.airflowignore
<https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/core-concepts/dags.html#airflowignore>`__
files in the DAG directories. Valid values are `regexp` or `glob`.

<a id="core.test_connection"></a>

### `test_connection`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `Disabled` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__TEST_CONNECTION` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

The ability to allow testing connections across Airflow UI, API and CLI.
Supported options: `Disabled`, `Enabled`, `Hidden`. Default: Disabled
Disabled - Disables the test connection functionality and disables the Test Connection button in UI.
Enabled - Enables the test connection functionality and shows the Test Connection button in UI.
Hidden - Disables the test connection functionality and hides the Test Connection button in UI.
Before setting this to Enabled, make sure that you review the users who are able to add/edit
connections and ensure they are trusted. Connection testing can be done maliciously leading to
undesired and insecure outcomes.
See `Airflow Security Model: Capabilities of authenticated UI users
<https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/security/security_model.html#capabilities-of-authenticated-ui-users>`__
for more details.

### `execution_api_server_url`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTION_API_SERVER_URL` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |
| Old name | `[workers] execution_api_server_url` (renamed in 3.0) |

The url of the execution api server. Default is `{BASE_URL}/execution/`
where `{BASE_URL}` is the base url of the API Server. If `{BASE_URL}` is not set
or is a relative path such as `/airflow`, it is prefixed with `http://localhost:{PORT}`,
where `{PORT}` is `[api] port`.

<a id="core.multi_team"></a>

### `multi_team`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__MULTI_TEAM` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Whether to run the Airflow environment in multi-team mode.
In this mode, different teams can have scoped access to their own resources while still sharing the
same underlying deployment.

<a id="core.team_name_cache_ttl"></a>

### `team_name_cache_ttl`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `30` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__TEAM_NAME_CACHE_TTL` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

Number of seconds a Dag's owning team (resolved from its bundle) is cached in memory before it
is looked up again. The team is read on every Dag authorization check, including the grid
endpoints which re-poll continuously, so caching it avoids repeated Team-table joins. A team
reassignment takes up to this many seconds to take effect, and different API server workers may
briefly disagree during that window. Set to `0` to disable caching.

<a id="core.rerun_with_latest_version"></a>

### `rerun_with_latest_version`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__CORE__RERUN_WITH_LATEST_VERSION` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Default value for whether cleared, rerun, or backfilled tasks should use
the latest bundle version. When set to True, reruns and backfills pick up
the latest code. When set to False, they use the original bundle version.
When unset, the fallback depends on the call site: False for clearing or
rerunning tasks, True for creating backfills (preserving the historical
defaults for each). Individual DAGs can override this with the
`rerun_with_latest_version` parameter.

## [database]

<a id="database.alembic_ini_file_path"></a>

### `alembic_ini_file_path`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `alembic.ini` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__ALEMBIC_INI_FILE_PATH` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

Path to the `alembic.ini` file. You can either provide the file path relative
to the Airflow home directory or the absolute path if it is located elsewhere.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_conn"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_conn`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `sqlite:///{AIRFLOW_HOME}/airflow.db` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |
| Old name | `[core] sql_alchemy_conn` (renamed in 3.0) |

The SQLAlchemy connection string to the metadata database.
SQLAlchemy supports many different database engines.
See: `Set up a Database Backend: Database URI
<https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/howto/set-up-database.html#database-uri>`__
for more details.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_conn_async"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_conn_async`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_ASYNC` |
| Example | `postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:airflow@postgres/airflow` |
| Added in | 3.1.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_ASYNC_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN_ASYNC_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

The SQLAlchemy connection string to the metadata database used for async connections.
If this is not set, Airflow automatically derives a string by converting `sql_alchemy_conn`.
Unfortunately, this conversion logic does not always work due to various incompatibilities
between sync and async db driver implementations. This sets the connection string directly
without any conversion instead.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_engine_args"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_engine_args`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_ENGINE_ARGS` |
| Example | `{"arg1": true}` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_ENGINE_ARGS_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_ENGINE_ARGS_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

Extra engine specific keyword args passed to SQLAlchemy's create_engine, as a JSON-encoded value

<a id="database.sql_engine_encoding"></a>

### `sql_engine_encoding`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `utf-8` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ENGINE_ENCODING` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The encoding for the databases

<a id="database.sql_engine_collation_for_ids"></a>

### `sql_engine_collation_for_ids`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ENGINE_COLLATION_FOR_IDS` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

Collation for `dag_id`, `task_id`, `key`, `external_executor_id` columns
in case they have different encoding.
By default this collation is the same as the database collation, however for `mysql` and `mariadb`
the default is `utf8mb3_bin` so that the index sizes of our index keys will not exceed
the maximum size of allowed index when collation is set to `utf8mb4` variant, see
[GitHub Issue Comment](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/17603#issuecomment-901121618)
for more details.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_pool_enabled"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_pool_enabled`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_POOL_ENABLED` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

If SQLAlchemy should pool database connections.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_pool_size"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_pool_size`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `5` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_POOL_SIZE` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The SQLAlchemy pool size is the maximum number of database connections
in the pool. 0 indicates no limit.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_max_overflow"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_max_overflow`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `10` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_MAX_OVERFLOW` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The maximum overflow size of the pool.
When the number of checked-out connections reaches the size set in pool_size,
additional connections will be returned up to this limit.
When those additional connections are returned to the pool, they are disconnected and discarded.
It follows then that the total number of simultaneous connections the pool will allow
is **pool_size** + **max_overflow**,
and the total number of "sleeping" connections the pool will allow is pool_size.
max_overflow can be set to `-1` to indicate no overflow limit;
no limit will be placed on the total number of concurrent connections. Defaults to `10`.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_pool_recycle"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_pool_recycle`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `1800` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_POOL_RECYCLE` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The SQLAlchemy pool recycle is the number of seconds a connection
can be idle in the pool before it is invalidated. This config does
not apply to sqlite. If the number of DB connections is ever exceeded,
a lower config value will allow the system to recover faster.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_pool_pre_ping"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_pool_pre_ping`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_POOL_PRE_PING` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

Check connection at the start of each connection pool checkout.
Typically, this is a simple statement like "SELECT 1".
See `SQLAlchemy Pooling: Disconnect Handling - Pessimistic
<https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/pooling.html#disconnect-handling-pessimistic>`__
for more details.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_schema"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_schema`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_SCHEMA` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

The schema to use for the metadata database.
SQLAlchemy supports databases with the concept of multiple schemas.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_connect_args"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_connect_args`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONNECT_ARGS` |
| Example | `airflow_local_settings.connect_args` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

Import path for connect args in SQLAlchemy. Defaults to an empty dict, except for
psycopg3 URLs, where Airflow defaults `prepare_threshold` to `None` so that
server-side statement preparation does not break under a transaction-pooling
connection pooler. Keys set here are merged over that default and win.
This is useful when you want to configure db engine args that SQLAlchemy won't parse
in connection string. This can be set by passing a dictionary containing the create engine parameters.
For more details about passing create engine parameters (keepalives variables, timeout etc)
in Postgres DB Backend see `Setting up a PostgreSQL Database
<https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/howto/set-up-database.html#setting-up-a-postgresql-database>`__
e.g `connect_args={"timeout":30}` can be defined in `airflow_local_settings.py` and
can be imported as shown below

*Changed in 3.1.0*: This configuration is only applied to synchronous engines, such as psycopg2.
See `sql_alchemy_connect_args_async`.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_connect_args_async"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_connect_args_async`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONNECT_ARGS_ASYNC` |
| Example | `airflow_local_settings.connect_args_async` |
| Added in | 3.1.0 |

Import path for connect args in SQLAlchemy. Defaults to an empty dict, except for
psycopg3 URLs -- see `sql_alchemy_connect_args`.
This is similar to `sql_alchemy_connect_args`, but only for async connections and must be a dict.

This is applied to the async engine only. If you opt in to the `asyncpg` driver behind
transaction-mode pgbouncer, set
`statement_cache_size` and `prepared_statement_cache_size` to `0` here to avoid "prepared
statement does not exist" errors. See the async driver section of the Postgres setup guide.

<a id="database.sql_alchemy_session_maker"></a>

### `sql_alchemy_session_maker`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_SESSION_MAKER` |
| Example | `airflow_local_settings._sessionmaker` |
| Added in | 2.10.0 |

Important Warning: Use of sql_alchemy_session_maker Highly Discouraged
Import path for function which returns 'sqlalchemy.orm.sessionmaker'.
Improper configuration of sql_alchemy_session_maker can lead to serious issues,
including data corruption, unrecoverable application crashes. Please review the SQLAlchemy
documentation for detailed guidance on proper configuration and best practices.

<a id="database.max_db_retries"></a>

### `max_db_retries`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `3` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__MAX_DB_RETRIES` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

Maximum number of attempts, including the first one, for operations retried on DB
operational errors. The default of 3 means one initial attempt plus up to 2 retries.
Not all transactions are retried, since retrying some of them can leave undesired state.

<a id="database.check_migrations"></a>

### `check_migrations`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__CHECK_MIGRATIONS` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

Whether to run alembic migrations during Airflow start up. Sometimes this operation can be expensive,
and the users can assert the correct version through other means (e.g. through a Helm chart).
Accepts `True` or `False`.

<a id="database.external_db_managers"></a>

### `external_db_managers`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__EXTERNAL_DB_MANAGERS` |
| Example | `airflow.providers.fab.auth_manager.models.db.FABDBManager` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Additional DB managers to include when migrating external tables in the Airflow
database, beyond those automatically discovered from installed providers.
The managers must inherit from BaseDBManager.

<a id="database.migration_batch_size"></a>

### `migration_batch_size`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `10000` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__DATABASE__MIGRATION_BATCH_SIZE` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The number of rows to process in each batch when performing a migration.
This is useful for large tables to avoid locking and failure due to query timeouts.

| | |

### `remote_logging`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__REMOTE_LOGGING` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Airflow can store logs remotely in AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage or Elastic Search.
Set this to `True` if you want to enable remote logging.

location. Depending on your remote logging service, this may only be used for
reading logs, not writing them.

Path to Google Credential JSON file. If omitted, authorization based on `the Application Default

<https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials>`__ will

<a id="logging.remote_base_log_folder"></a>

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |

Storage bucket URL for remote logging

<a id="logging.remote_task_handler_kwargs"></a>

### `remote_task_handler_kwargs`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__REMOTE_TASK_HANDLER_KWARGS` |
| Example | `{"delete_local_copy": true}` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__REMOTE_TASK_HANDLER_KWARGS_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__REMOTE_TASK_HANDLER_KWARGS_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

The remote_task_handler_kwargs param is loaded into a dictionary and passed to the `__init__`
of remote task handler and it overrides the values provided by Airflow config. For example if you set
`delete_local_logs=False` and you provide `{"delete_local_copy": true}`, then the local
log files will be deleted after they are uploaded to remote location.

<a id="logging.logging_level"></a>

### `logging_level`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `INFO` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOGGING_LEVEL` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Logging level.

Individual loggers can be set at a different level with the `config:logging__namespace_levels`
option.

Supported values: `CRITICAL`, `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`.

<a id="logging.namespace_levels"></a>

### `namespace_levels`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__NAMESPACE_LEVELS` |
| Example | `sqlalchemy=INFO sqlalchemy.engine=DEBUG, botocor` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Set the log level for individual named loggers.

A very common convention in Python is to use the module name as the name of the logger from which log
messages originate. This config option gives us the ability to set log levels for those loggers
easily.

The format of this variable is a series of `<logger>=<level>` pairs, separated by whitespace or
commas.

Each level is one of the possible values to `logging_level`.

The logger names are viewable in task logs (as the "source" attribute), or in server components by
including `%(name)s` in your format string, or in the between `[]` after the message in the
default format.

<a id="logging.celery_logging_level"></a>

### `celery_logging_level`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__CELERY_LOGGING_LEVEL` |
| Added in | 2.3.0 |

Logging level for celery. If not set, it uses the value of logging_level

Supported values: `CRITICAL`, `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`.

<a id="logging.fab_logging_level"></a>

### `fab_logging_level`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `WARNING` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__FAB_LOGGING_LEVEL` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Logging level for Flask-appbuilder UI.

Supported values: `CRITICAL`, `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`.

<a id="logging.json_logs"></a>

### `json_logs`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__JSON_LOGS` |
| Example | `True` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Enable JSON-structured logging for all output. When `True`, every log line emitted by
the process is a single-line JSON object (including HTTP access logs from the API server).
Recommended for production / cloud-native deployments where logs are collected by a log
aggregator.

<a id="logging.task_logs_to_stdout"></a>

### `task_logs_to_stdout`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__TASK_LOGS_TO_STDOUT` |
| Example | `True` |
| Added in | 3.4.0 |

Also forward task subprocess stdout/stderr to the worker's own stdout, so task logs reach
a container-level log collector (e.g. Kubernetes/Loki) in addition to the task-log handler
and the UI. This is not a global switch: it is only consulted when a caller leaves
`subprocess_logs_to_stdout` out of `BaseExecutor.run_workload`. Executors that already pass
`True` explicitly (the LocalExecutor and the per-task entrypoint used by the Kubernetes, ECS,
Batch and Lambda executors) always forward task logs to stdout and ignore this setting. Currently
it is read by the Celery worker (which resolves `[celery] task_logs_to_stdout` first, then this
setting) and by the Edge3 worker's fork path on Airflow 3.4+.

| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Logging level for uvicorn (API server and serve-logs).

| Example | `my.path.default_local_settings.LOGGING_CONFIG` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Dotted import path to a `logging.config.dictConfig` dict. The
`_class` suffix is historical — the target is a dict, not a class.

Airflow also reads two optional module-level attributes from the
enclosing module: `REMOTE_TASK_LOG` and `DEFAULT_REMOTE_CONN_ID`,
used to drive remote task-log read-back. See `write-logs-advanced`.

| :--- | :--- |

| Type | string |

| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Flag to enable/disable Colored logs in Console
Colour the logs when the controlling terminal is a TTY.

<a id="logging.log_format"></a>

### `log_format`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOG_FORMAT` |
| Example | `[%%(asctime)s] {{%%(filename)s:%%(lineno)d}} %%(levelname)s - %%(message)s` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Format of Log line

*Changed in 3.1.0*: This can now contain color escape sequences `%(blue)s` etc which will only
result in colours if `config:logging__colored_console_log` is true.

<a id="logging.callsite_parameters"></a>

### `callsite_parameters`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `filename,lineno` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__CALLSITE_PARAMETERS` |
| Added in | 3.1.0 |

A comma separated list of information about the callsite (such as line number of filename etc) of
logger calls to include in each message.

See `structlog.processors.CallsiteParameter` for the possible values.The values should be the
constant names (`FUNC_NAME`) or the values (`func_name`)

Including these in a log message adds a lot to the usability to the logs, but collecting these has a
(tiny) cost -- if you are super concerned with eking out every last ounce of performance you could
turn these off (by setting this value to an empty string)

Defines the format of log messages for simple logging configuration

<a id="logging.log_formatter_class"></a>

### `log_formatter_class`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `airflow.utils.log.timezone_aware.TimezoneAware` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOG_FORMATTER_CLASS` |
| Added in | 2.3.4 |

Determines the formatter class used by Airflow for structuring its log messages
The default formatter class is timezone-aware, which means that timestamps attached to log entries
will be adjusted to reflect the local timezone of the Airflow instance.
Note: This setting does NOT affect component logs (scheduler, api-server, triggerer, etc.) since
those use structlog directly. Use `log_timestamp_format` to control timestamps for those logs.

<a id="logging.log_timestamp_format"></a>

### `log_timestamp_format`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `iso` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT` |
| Example | `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` |
| Added in | 3.0.4 |

Timestamp format for component logs (scheduler, api-server, triggerer, etc.).
Use `iso` for ISO 8601 format (default), or a Python strftime format string
such as `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S`.
Note: This setting only applies to component logs rendered via structlog.
Task/DAG logs use `log_format` instead.

<a id="logging.secret_mask_adapter"></a>

### `secret_mask_adapter`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__SECRET_MASK_ADAPTER` |
| Example | `urllib.parse.quote` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

An import path to a function to add adaptations of each secret added with
`airflow.sdk.execution_time.secrets_masker.mask_secret` to be masked in log messages.
The given function is expected to require a single parameter: the secret to be adapted.
It may return a single adaptation of the secret or an iterable of adaptations to each be
masked as secrets. The original secret will be masked as well as any adaptations returned.

The minimum length of a secret to be masked in log messages.

<a id="logging.worker_log_server_port"></a>

### `worker_log_server_port`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `8793` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__WORKER_LOG_SERVER_PORT` |
| Added in | 2.2.0 |

When you start an Airflow worker, Airflow starts a tiny web server
subprocess to serve the workers local log files to the airflow main
web server, who then builds pages and sends them to users. This defines
the port on which the logs are served. It needs to be unused, and open
visible from the main web server to connect into the workers.

<a id="logging.trigger_log_server_port"></a>

### `trigger_log_server_port`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `8794` |

| Added in | 2.6.0 |

Port to serve logs from for triggerer.

<a id="logging.interleave_timestamp_parser"></a>

### `interleave_timestamp_parser`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__INTERLEAVE_TIMESTAMP_PARSER` |
| Example | `path.to.my_func` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

We must parse timestamps to interleave logs between trigger and task.  To do so,
we need to parse timestamps in log files. In case your log format is non-standard,
you may provide import path to callable which takes a string log line and returns
the timestamp (datetime.datetime compatible).

<a id="logging.file_task_handler_new_folder_permissions"></a>

### `file_task_handler_new_folder_permissions`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `0o775` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__FILE_TASK_HANDLER_NEW_FOLDER_PERMISSIONS` |
| Example | `0o775` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

Permissions in the form or of octal string as understood by chmod. The permissions are important
when you use impersonation, when logs are written by a different user than airflow. The most secure
way of configuring it in this case is to add both users to the same group and make it the default
group of both users. Group-writeable logs are default in airflow, but you might decide that you are
OK with having the logs other-writeable, in which case you should set it to `0o777`. You might
decide to add more security if you do not use impersonation and change it to `0o755` to make it
only owner-writeable. You can also make it just readable only for owner by changing it to `0o700`
if all the access (read/write) for your logs happens from the same user.

<a id="logging.file_task_handler_new_file_permissions"></a>

### `file_task_handler_new_file_permissions`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `0o664` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__FILE_TASK_HANDLER_NEW_FILE_PERMISSIONS` |
| Example | `0o664` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |

Permissions in the form or of octal string as understood by chmod. The permissions are important
when you use impersonation, when logs are written by a different user than airflow. The most secure
way of configuring it in this case is to add both users to the same group and make it the default
group of both users. Group-writeable logs are default in airflow, but you might decide that you are
OK with having the logs other-writeable, in which case you should set it to `0o666`. You might
decide to add more security if you do not use impersonation and change it to `0o644` to make it
only owner-writeable. You can also make it just readable only for owner by changing it to `0o600`
if all the access (read/write) for your logs happens from the same user.

<a id="logging.celery_stdout_stderr_separation"></a>

### `celery_stdout_stderr_separation`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__CELERY_STDOUT_STDERR_SEPARATION` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

By default Celery sends all logs into stderr.
If enabled any previous logging handlers will get *removed*.
With this option AirFlow will create new handlers
and send low level logs like INFO and WARNING to stdout,
while sending higher severity logs to stderr.

color in UI

color in UI

[StatsD](https://github.com/statsd/statsd) integration settings.

<a id="metrics.metrics_allow_list"></a>

| | |
| :--- | :--- |

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |

from being emitted.
If `[metrics] metrics_allow_list` and `[metrics] metrics_block_list` are both configured,

Legacy names contain variables such as dag_id and task_id,
while the new names set these variables inside tags.

### `statsd_on`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__METRICS__STATSD_ON` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Enables sending metrics to StatsD.

<a id="metrics.statsd_ipv6"></a>

### `statsd_ipv6`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__METRICS__STATSD_IPV6` |

Enables the statsd host to be resolved into IPv6 address

### `statsd_port`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `8125` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__METRICS__STATSD_PORT` |
| Added in | 2.0.0 |

Specifies the port on which the StatsD daemon (or server) is listening to.
Ignored when `statsd_socket_path` is set.

<a id="metrics.statsd_socket_path"></a>

### `statsd_socket_path`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__METRICS__STATSD_SOCKET_PATH` |
| Example | `/var/run/statsd/statsd.sock` |
| Added in | 3.4.0 |

Path to a Unix Domain Socket used to submit metrics, instead of `statsd_host`
and `statsd_port`. Applies to both the StatsD and Datadog backends. Takes
precedence over `statsd_host` / `statsd_port` when set. For the Datadog
backend (`statsd_datadog_enabled = True`) a plain path or a `unix://` /
`unixgram://` / `unixstream://` URL is accepted; for the StatsD backend a
plain filesystem path is expected. Note that `statsd_ipv6` has no effect when
this option is set.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |

Defines the namespace for all metrics sent from Airflow to StatsD

| | |
| :--- | :--- |

## [secrets]

<a id="secrets.backend"></a>

### `backend`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND` |
| Example | `airflow.providers.amazon.aws.secrets.systems_manager.SystemsManagerParameterStoreBackend` |
| Added in | 1.10.10 |

Full class name of secrets backend to enable (will precede env vars and metastore in search path)

<a id="secrets.backend_kwargs"></a>

### `backend_kwargs`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARGS` |
| Added in | 1.10.10 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARGS_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARGS_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

The backend_kwargs param is loaded into a dictionary and passed to `__init__`
of secrets backend class. See documentation for the secrets backend you are using.
JSON is expected.

Example for AWS Systems Manager ParameterStore:
`{"connections_prefix": "/airflow/connections", "profile_name": "default"}`

You can also set individual kwargs via `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARG__<KEY>=value`
environment variables. Per-key variables override the same key in this JSON setting.
Values are raw strings (not JSON-parsed).

<a id="secrets.use_cache"></a>

### `use_cache`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__USE_CACHE` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

**Note:** |experimental|

Enables local caching of Variables, when parsing DAGs only.
Using this option can make dag parsing faster if Variables are used in top level code, at the expense
of longer propagation time for changes.
Please note that this cache concerns only the DAG parsing step. There is no caching in place when DAG
tasks are run.

<a id="secrets.cache_ttl_seconds"></a>

### `cache_ttl_seconds`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `900` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SECRETS__CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` |
| Added in | 2.7.0 |

**Note:** |experimental|

When the cache is enabled, this is the duration for which we consider an entry in the cache to be
valid. Entries are refreshed if they are older than this many seconds.
It means that when the cache is enabled, this is the maximum amount of time you need to wait to see a
Variable change take effect.

## [api]

<a id="api.instance_name"></a>

### `instance_name`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__INSTANCE_NAME` |
| Added in | 2.1.0 |
| Old name | `[webserver] instance_name` (renamed in 3.1.0) |

Sets a custom homepage heading and site title for all Airflow UI pages.
If set, the Dashboard will display this value instead of the default
"Welcome" message.

<a id="api.theme"></a>

### `theme`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__THEME` |
| Example | `{       "tokens": {         "colors": {           "brand": {             "50": { "value": "oklch(0.971 0.013 17.38)" },             "100": { "value": "oklch(0.936 0.032 17.717)" },             "200": { "value": "oklch(0.885 0.062 18.334)" },             "300": { "value": "oklch(0.808 0.114 19.571)" },             "400": { "value": "oklch(0.704 0.191 22.216)" },             "500": { "value": "oklch(0.637 0.237 25.331)" },             "600": { "value": "oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)" },             "700": { "value": "oklch(0.505 0.213 27.518)" },             "800": { "value": "oklch(0.444 0.177 26.899)" },             "900": { "value": "oklch(0.396 0.141 25.723)" },             "950": { "value": "oklch(0.258 0.092 26.042)" }           }         }       }     } ` |

JSON config to customize the Chakra UI theme.
Supports `brand` color customization, `globalCss`, and optional navigation icons `icon`
(for light mode) and `icon_dark_mode` (for dark mode). Icons must be SVG files and can be
either absolute http(s) URLs or app-relative paths starting with `/`.

Must supply `50`-`950` OKLCH color values for `brand` color.

For usage see `customizing-ui-theme`

.. important::
  `oklch(l c h)` must follow next format:

  - l (lightness) : `float` Must be between 0 and 1
  - c (chroma) : `float` Must be between 0 and 0.5
  - h (hue) : `float` Must be between 0 and 360

Note: As shown below, you can split your json config over multiple lines by indenting.
See configparser documentation for an example:
https://docs.python.org/3/library/configparser.html#supported-ini-file-structure.

<a id="api.enable_swagger_ui"></a>

### `enable_swagger_ui`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `True` |
| Type | boolean |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__ENABLE_SWAGGER_UI` |
| Added in | 2.6.0 |
| Old name | `[webserver] enable_swagger_ui` (renamed in 3.0.2) |

Boolean for running SwaggerUI in the webserver.

<a id="api.regexp_query_timeout"></a>

### `regexp_query_timeout`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `0` |
| Type | float |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__REGEXP_QUERY_TIMEOUT` |
| Added in | 3.4.0 |

Timeout, in seconds, for regular-expression based query filters in the API. Fractional
values are allowed (e.g. `0.5`). This single value both enables the feature and bounds its
runtime: a value of `0` (the default) disables regexp filtering entirely, and any positive
value enables it while capping how long such a query may run.

When enabled, it allows additional filtering features that require database-side regexp
matching, such as the `partition_key_regexp_pattern` filter on `GET /assets/events`
and on the Execution API asset-event endpoints. It is disabled by default for security
reasons: a user-supplied regular expression is passed to the database's own regex engine,
which is a Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vector: a crafted pattern can
force the engine into pathological backtracking and consume database backend CPU.

The timeout is the primary runtime mitigation for that risk: it is enforced as a
transaction-local `statement_timeout` on PostgreSQL and as the session `max_execution_time`
on MySQL, so a pathological pattern is aborted instead of pinning a database backend. Keep it
as low as your legitimate queries allow. Coupling the on/off switch with the timeout
intentionally makes it impossible to enable regexp filtering without a runtime bound in place.

<a id="api.secret_key"></a>

### `secret_key`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `{SECRET_KEY}` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__SECRET_KEY` |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__API__SECRET_KEY_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__API__SECRET_KEY_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |
| Old name | `[webserver] secret_key` (renamed in 3.0.2) |

Secret key used to run your api server. It should be as random as possible. However, when running
more than 1 instances of the api, make sure all of them use the same `secret_key` otherwise
one of them will error with "CSRF session token is missing".
The api key is also used to authorize requests to Celery workers when logs are retrieved.
The token generated using the secret key has a short expiry time though - make sure that time on
ALL the machines that you run airflow components on is synchronized (for example using ntpd)
otherwise you might get "forbidden" errors when the logs are accessed.

<a id="api.expose_config"></a>

### `expose_config`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__EXPOSE_CONFIG` |
| Old name | `[webserver] expose_config` (renamed in 3.0.1) |

Expose the configuration file in the web server. Set to `True` to expose configuration with
sensitive values always masked. The deprecated value `non-sensitive-only` is treated the same as
`True` for backward compatibility. `False` hides the configuration completely.

<a id="api.expose_stacktrace"></a>

### `expose_stacktrace`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `False` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__EXPOSE_STACKTRACE` |

Expose stacktrace in the web server

<a id="api.dag_cache_size"></a>

### `dag_cache_size`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `64` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__DAG_CACHE_SIZE` |
| Added in | 3.2.2 |

Max number of deserialized SerializedDAG objects the API server keeps in memory. Set to 0 for no
size limit, leaving eviction to `dag_cache_ttl`. Setting both this and `dag_cache_ttl` to 0
disables eviction, so the API server retains every deserialized Dag it loads until restart, matching
the behavior before 3.2.2.

The cache is keyed by Dag version ID, so lookups by Dag ID
(e.g., viewing a Dag's details) always query the database for the latest
version, but the deserialized result is cached for subsequent
version-specific lookups.

<a id="api.dag_cache_ttl"></a>

### `dag_cache_ttl`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `3600` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__DAG_CACHE_TTL` |
| Added in | 3.2.2 |

Seconds a deserialized SerializedDAG stays in the API server's cache, applied whether or
not `dag_cache_size` sets a size limit. After this time the Dag is re-fetched from the
database on next access. Set to 0 to disable TTL, leaving eviction to the
`dag_cache_size` LRU policy.

An entry's TTL is refreshed only when the entry is checked against the database after
`[core] min_serialized_dag_update_interval`, not on every request. If the TTL is shorter
than that interval, even frequently requested entries can expire and reload between
checks. `dag_cache_size` remains the only hard ceiling on memory.

Note: this does not govern staleness. A Dag update that creates a new version is picked
up immediately, because the new version is a different cache key. A version rewritten in
place is re-checked against its current `dag_hash` once
`[core] min_serialized_dag_update_interval` has elapsed since the entry was last
validated, so that option bounds how long a rewritten version can be served stale.

should contain the API server endpoint.

| Old name | `[webserver] workers` (renamed in 3.0) |

Number of workers to run on the API server. Should be roughly equal to the number of cpu cores
available. If you need to scale the API server, strongly consider deploying multiple API servers
instead of increasing the number of workers; See https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/52270.

<a id="api.worker_timeout"></a>

### `worker_timeout`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `120` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__WORKER_TIMEOUT` |
| Old name | `[webserver] web_server_worker_timeout` (renamed in 3.0) |

Number of seconds the API server waits before timing out on a worker

<a id="api.server_type"></a>

### `server_type`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `uvicorn` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__SERVER_TYPE` |
| Example | `gunicorn` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

The server type to use for the API server. Options are:

- `uvicorn`: Default. Uses uvicorn directly. Simple setup, but does not
  support rolling worker restarts with `worker_refresh_interval` because
  uvicorn's multiprocess mode has no master process when workers=1 and
  SIGTTOU kills the newest worker (LIFO), not oldest.

- `gunicorn`: Uses gunicorn with uvicorn workers. Supports rolling worker
  restarts via `worker_refresh_interval`. Requires `apache-airflow-core[gunicorn]`
  extra. Gunicorn always has master/worker architecture and SIGTTOU kills
  the oldest worker (FIFO) which is correct for rolling restarts.

Note: When using gunicorn, workers share memory via copy-on-write after fork,
reducing overall memory usage. With uvicorn multiprocess mode, each worker
loads everything independently with no memory sharing.

<a id="api.worker_refresh_interval"></a>

### `worker_refresh_interval`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `0` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__WORKER_REFRESH_INTERVAL` |
| Example | `43200` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Number of seconds between rolling worker refreshes for the API server.
When enabled, workers are periodically restarted using a rolling restart
pattern (new workers spawn before old ones are killed) to prevent memory
accumulation while maintaining zero downtime.

Set to 0 to disable worker refresh (default).

This option only works when `server_type = gunicorn`. With uvicorn,
this setting is ignored because uvicorn's SIGTTOU kills the newest worker
(LIFO order) rather than oldest, which defeats rolling restart purposes.

<a id="api.worker_refresh_batch_size"></a>

### `worker_refresh_batch_size`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `1` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__WORKER_REFRESH_BATCH_SIZE` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Number of workers to refresh at a time during rolling restarts.
Higher values refresh faster but temporarily use more resources.

Only used when `worker_refresh_interval > 0` and `server_type = gunicorn`.

<a id="api.log_config"></a>

### `log_config`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__LOG_CONFIG` |
| Example | `path/to/logging_config.yaml` |
| Old name | `[api] access_logfile` (renamed in 3.1.0) |

Path to the logging configuration file for the uvicorn server.
If not set, the default uvicorn logging configuration will be used.

<a id="api.log_stream_buffer_size"></a>

### `log_stream_buffer_size`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `500` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__LOG_STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE` |
| Added in | 3.2.0 |

Number of log lines to buffer before flushing to the client when streaming task logs
in NDJSON format. Larger values reduce HTTP overhead but increase time-to-first-byte.

| Old name | `[webserver] web_server_ssl_cert` (renamed in 3.0) |

Paths to the SSL certificate and key for the api server. When both are
provided SSL will be enabled. This does not change the api server port.
The same SSL certificate will also be loaded into the worker to enable
it to be trusted when a self-signed certificate is used.

<a id="api.ssl_key"></a>

| Old name | `[webserver] web_server_ssl_key` (renamed in 3.0) |

Paths to the SSL certificate and key for the api server. When both are

Path to the SSL CA file for the api server. Defaults to None.

<a id="api.ssl_cert_reqs"></a>

Enable ssl certificate verification on the api server.
See https://docs.python.org/3/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext.verify_mode

<a id="api.ssl_ciphers"></a>

<a id="api.maximum_page_limit"></a>

Used to set the maximum page limit for API requests. If limit passed as param

<a id="api.fallback_page_limit"></a>

| | |

| Added in | 2.0.0 |
| Old name | `[api] page_size` (renamed in 3.2.0) |

Used to set the default page limit when limit param is zero or not provided in API

<a id="api.access_control_allow_headers"></a>

### `access_control_allow_headers`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_HEADERS` |
| Added in | 2.1.0 |

Used in response to a preflight request to indicate which HTTP
headers can be used when making the actual request. This header is
the server side response to the browser's
Access-Control-Request-Headers header.

<a id="api.access_control_allow_methods"></a>

### `access_control_allow_methods`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_METHODS` |
| Added in | 2.1.0 |

Specifies the method or methods allowed when accessing the resource.

<a id="api.access_control_allow_origins"></a>

### `access_control_allow_origins`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGINS` |
| Added in | 2.2.0 |

Indicates whether the response can be shared with requesting code from the given origins.
Separate URLs with space. Wildcard (`*`) is not allowed: Airflow's API requires
credentialed CORS, which is incompatible with a wildcard origin per the CORS spec, and
browsers reject any response that combines the two. List exact origins instead
(for example `https://airflow.mycompany.com`).

<a id="api.access_control_allow_origin_regex"></a>

### `access_control_allow_origin_regex`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API__ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGIN_REGEX` |
| Added in | 3.4.0 |

A regex matched against the request `Origin` to decide whether the response can be shared,
as an alternative to listing exact origins in `access_control_allow_origins`. Useful when
the allowed origins are dynamic (for example per-branch preview deployments). The matched
origin is echoed back rather than `*`, so it stays compatible with the credentialed CORS
Airflow's API requires. Example: `https://.*\\.mycompany\\.com`.

## [workers]

Configuration related to workers that run Airflow tasks.

<a id="workers.secrets_backend"></a>

### `secrets_backend`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND` |
| Example | `airflow.providers.amazon.aws.secrets.systems_manager.SystemsManagerParameterStoreBackend` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Full class name of secrets backend to enable for workers (will precede env vars backend)

<a id="workers.secrets_backend_kwargs"></a>

### `secrets_backend_kwargs`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND_KWARGS` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND_KWARGS_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND_KWARGS_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

The secrets_backend_kwargs param is loaded into a dictionary and passed to `__init__`
of secrets backend class. See documentation for the secrets backend you are using.
JSON is expected.

Example for AWS Systems Manager ParameterStore:
`{"connections_prefix": "/airflow/connections", "profile_name": "default"}`

You can also set individual kwargs via `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND_KWARG__<KEY>=value`
environment variables. Per-key variables override the same key in this JSON setting.
Values are raw strings (not JSON-parsed).

<a id="workers.state_store_backend"></a>

### `state_store_backend`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(empty)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__STATE_STORE_BACKEND` |
| Example | `mypackage.state.S3StateBackend` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

Full class name of a custom worker-side store backend. When set, task store values are
routed through this backend so large payloads or credentialed storage stay on worker
infrastructure. The Execution API still records a reference string in the database.

Leave empty (default) to use the standard path through the task sdk supervisor.

<a id="workers.min_heartbeat_interval"></a>

### `min_heartbeat_interval`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `5` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__MIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The minimum interval (in seconds) at which the worker checks the task instance's
heartbeat status with the API server to confirm it is still alive.

<a id="workers.max_failed_heartbeats"></a>

### `max_failed_heartbeats`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `30` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__MAX_FAILED_HEARTBEATS` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The maximum number of consecutive failed heartbeats before terminating the task instance process.

Unlike other calls to the execution API, heartbeats are not retried. This setting and
`min_heartbeat_interval` together determine how long a worker tolerates an unreachable API server
before killing running tasks.

<a id="workers.execution_api_retries"></a>

### `execution_api_retries`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `5` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__EXECUTION_API_RETRIES` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The maximum number of retry attempts to the execution API server.

Note that task instance heartbeats are not retried.

<a id="workers.execution_api_retry_wait_min"></a>

### `execution_api_retry_wait_min`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `1.0` |
| Type | float |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__EXECUTION_API_RETRY_WAIT_MIN` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The minimum amount of time (in seconds) to wait before retrying a failed API request.

<a id="workers.execution_api_retry_wait_max"></a>

### `execution_api_retry_wait_max`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `90.0` |
| Type | float |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__EXECUTION_API_RETRY_WAIT_MAX` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The maximum amount of time (in seconds) to wait before retrying a failed API request.

<a id="workers.execution_api_timeout"></a>

### `execution_api_timeout`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `5.0` |
| Type | float |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__EXECUTION_API_TIMEOUT` |
| Added in | 3.1.1 |

The timeout (in seconds) for HTTP requests from workers to the Execution API server.
This controls how long a worker will wait for a response from the API server before
timing out. Increase this value if you experience timeout errors under high load.

<a id="workers.socket_cleanup_timeout"></a>

### `socket_cleanup_timeout`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `60.0` |
| Type | float |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SOCKET_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT` |
| Added in | 3.0.3 |

Number of seconds to wait after a task process exits before forcibly closing any
remaining communication sockets. This helps prevent the task supervisor from hanging
indefinitely due to missed EOF signals.

<a id="workers.missing_dag_retries"></a>

### `missing_dag_retries`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `3` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__MISSING_DAG_RETRIES` |
| Added in | 3.1.7 |
| Old name | `[workers] missing_dag_retires` (renamed in 3.1.8) |

Maximum number of times a task will be rescheduled if the worker fails to
load the Dag or task definition during startup.

This situation can occur due to transient infrastructure issues such as
missing Dag files, temporary filesystem or network problems, or bundle
synchronization delays. Rescheduling in this case does not count as a
task retry.

Set this value to 0 to disable rescheduling and fail the task immediately
on startup failures.

<a id="workers.missing_dag_retry_delay"></a>

### `missing_dag_retry_delay`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `60` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__WORKERS__MISSING_DAG_RETRY_DELAY` |
| Added in | 3.1.7 |

Delay in seconds before a task is rescheduled after a worker startup
failure caused by an inability to load the Dag or task definition.

This delay is applied when the task runner requests the scheduler to
reschedule the task instance in UP_FOR_RESCHEDULE state.

## [sdk]

Settings for non-Python SDK runtime coordination

<a id="sdk.coordinators"></a>

### `coordinators`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SDK__COORDINATORS` |
| Example | `{   "jdk-17": {     "classpath": "airflow.sdk.coordinators.java.JavaCoordinator",     "kwargs": {       "task_handler_bundle_name": "java-task-handlers",       "java_executable": "/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk/bin/java",       "jvm_args": ["-Xmx1024m"]     },     "extra": {       "pod_template_file": "/opt/airflow/pod_templates/java.yaml",       "worker_container_repository": "apache/airflow",       "worker_container_tag": "3.3.0"     }   },   "go-sdk": {     "classpath": "airflow.sdk.coordinators.executable.ExecutableCoordinator",     "kwargs": {       "task_handler_bundle_name": "go-task-handlers"     }   } } ` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

JSON object mapping of coordinator keys to coordinator definitions.

Each value is an object with `classpath` and optional `kwargs`.
`classpath` is resolved via `import_string` and constructed with
`kwargs` on first use.  Entries are
independent instances, so the same `classpath` can be configured
multiple times under different names with different `kwargs` (for
example, two `JavaCoordinator` instances pinned to different JDK
versions).

The language SDK coordinators read the task handlers for the
`@task.stub` tasks of a Python Dag from the Dag bundle named by the
`task_handler_bundle_name` kwarg. Dags defined natively in a language
SDK do not use it. It must name a bundle in
`[dag_processor] dag_bundle_config_list` and is checked when this
option is loaded. When it is unset, a task reads its handlers from its
own Dag bundle.

The Dag processor needs this option too, with the language runtime the
coordinator starts and the files of that Dag bundle, because it checks
the stub tasks of each Python Dag against the task handlers those files
register. The API server does not need it.

An entry may also carry an optional `extra` object for additional
information associated with the coordinator that the coordinator itself
does not receive; other components read it as needed. For example,
KubernetesExecutor reads `extra.pod_template_file` to launch a queue's
worker pod from a specific pod template, and
`extra.worker_container_repository` + `extra.worker_container_tag` to
override the worker base image for that queue (both are required).

<a id="sdk.queue_to_coordinator"></a>

### `queue_to_coordinator`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SDK__QUEUE_TO_COORDINATOR` |
| Example | `{"legacy-java": "jdk-11", "modern-java": "jdk-17"}` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

JSON mapping of queue names to a coordinator key from
`[sdk] coordinators`.

This mapping is checked to route a task to a configured coordinator
instance based on its queue.  An entry in this mapping is needed if
tasks of a queue should be handled by a custom coordinator instead of
the default Python task-running mechanism.

<a id="sdk.dag_bundle_to_coordinator"></a>

### `dag_bundle_to_coordinator`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__SDK__DAG_BUNDLE_TO_COORDINATOR` |
| Example | `{"dags-folder": "java-native"}` |
| Added in | 3.4.0 |

JSON object mapping a Dag bundle name to one key of `[sdk] coordinators`. It picks the coordinator
that parses the bundle's native Dag files when several coordinators of that runtime are configured.

With one coordinator of a runtime, that coordinator parses the runtime's native Dag files in every
Dag bundle, and this option is not read. With several, a bundle that holds such files must map to
one of them, otherwise each file fails to parse with an import error. A bundle maps to one
coordinator, so it can hold native Dag files of only one runtime that has several coordinators.
Tasks do not read this option; `queue_to_coordinator` routes them.

## [api_auth]

Settings relating to authentication on the Airflow APIs

<a id="api_auth.jwt_audience"></a>

### `jwt_audience`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_AUDIENCE` |
| Example | `my-unique-airflow-id` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The audience claim to use when generating and validating JWTs for the API.

This variable can be a single value, or a comma-separated string, in which case the first value is the
one that will be used when generating, and the others are accepted at validation time.

Not required, but strongly encouraged.

See also `config:execution_api__jwt_audience`

<a id="api_auth.jwt_expiration_time"></a>

### `jwt_expiration_time`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `86400` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_EXPIRATION_TIME` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Number in seconds until the JWTs used for authentication expires. When the token expires,
all API calls using this token will fail on authentication.

Make sure that time on ALL the machines that you run airflow components on is synchronized
(for example using ntpd) otherwise you might get "forbidden" errors.

See also `config:execution_api__jwt_expiration_time`

<a id="api_auth.jwt_cli_expiration_time"></a>

### `jwt_cli_expiration_time`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `3600` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_CLI_EXPIRATION_TIME` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Number in seconds until the JWTs used for authentication expires for CLI commands.
When the token expires, all CLI calls using this token will fail on authentication.

Make sure that time on ALL the machines that you run airflow components on is synchronized
(for example using ntpd) otherwise you might get "forbidden" errors.

<a id="api_auth.jwt_secret"></a>

### `jwt_secret`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `{JWT_SECRET_KEY}` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_SECRET` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |
| Sensitive | yes: also `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_SECRET_CMD` and `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_SECRET_SECRET`; hidden in `airflow config list` |

Secret key used to encode and decode JWTs to authenticate to public and private APIs.

It should be as random as possible. This key must be consistent across all components that
generate or validate JWT tokens (Scheduler, API Server). For improved security, consider
using asymmetric keys (`jwt_private_key_path`) instead, which allow you to restrict the
signing key to only the components that need to generate tokens.

For security-sensitive deployments, pass this value via environment variable
(`AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_SECRET`) rather than storing it in a configuration file, and
restrict it to only the components that need it.

Mutually exclusive with `jwt_private_key_path`.

<a id="api_auth.jwt_private_key_path"></a>

### `jwt_private_key_path`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` |
| Example | `/path/to/private_key.pem` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The path to a file containing a PEM-encoded private key use when generating Task Identity tokens in
the executor.

Mutually exclusive with `jwt_secret`.

<a id="api_auth.jwt_algorithm"></a>

### `jwt_algorithm`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_ALGORITHM` |
| Example | `"EdDSA" or "HS512"` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The algorithm name use when generating and validating JWT Task Identities.

This value must be appropriate for the given private key type.

If this is not specified Airflow makes some guesses as what algorithm is best based on the key type.

("HS512" if `jwt_secret` is set, otherwise a key-type specific guess)

<a id="api_auth.jwt_kid"></a>

### `jwt_kid`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_KID` |
| Example | `my-key-id` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The Key ID to place in header when generating JWTs. Not used in the validation path.

If this is not specified the RFC7638 thumbprint of the private key will be used.

Ignored when `jwt_secret` is used.

<a id="api_auth.trusted_jwks_url"></a>

### `trusted_jwks_url`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__TRUSTED_JWKS_URL` |
| Example | `"/path/to/public-jwks.json" or "https://my-issuer/.well-known/jwks.json"` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The public signing keys of Task Execution token issuers to trust. It must contain the public key
related to `jwt_private_key_path` else tasks will be unlikely to execute successfully.

Can be a local file path (without the `file://` prefix) or an http or https URL.

If a remote URL is given it will be polled periodically for changes.

Mutually exclusive with `jwt_secret`.

If a `jwt_private_key_path` is given but this settings is not set then the private key will be
trusted. If this is provided it is your responsibility to ensure that the private key used for
generation is in this list.

<a id="api_auth.jwt_issuer"></a>

### `jwt_issuer`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_ISSUER` |
| Example | `http://my-airflow.mycompany.com` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Issuer of the JWT. This becomes the `iss` claim of generated tokens, and is validated on incoming
requests.

Ideally this should be unique per individual airflow deployment

Not required, but strongly recommended to be set.

See also `config:api_auth__jwt_audience`

<a id="api_auth.jwt_leeway"></a>

### `jwt_leeway`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `10` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_LEEWAY` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Number of seconds leeway in validating expiry time of JWTs to account for clock skew between
client and server

## [execution_api]

Settings related to the Execution API server.

The ExecutionAPI also uses a lot of settings from the `config:api_auth` section.

<a id="execution_api.jwt_expiration_time"></a>

### `jwt_expiration_time`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `600` |
| Type | integer |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__EXECUTION_API__JWT_EXPIRATION_TIME` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

Number in seconds until the JWT used for authentication expires. When the token expires,
all API calls using this token will fail on authentication.

Make sure that time on ALL the machines that you run airflow components on is synchronized
(for example using ntpd) otherwise you might get "forbidden" errors.

<a id="execution_api.otel_trace_propagation"></a>

### `otel_trace_propagation`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `only-authenticated` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__EXECUTION_API__OTEL_TRACE_PROPAGATION` |
| Added in | 3.3.0 |

Controls when W3C trace context (`traceparent`/`tracestate`) is extracted from
incoming Execution API requests and attached to the OpenTelemetry context.

`only-authenticated` (default): trace context is extracted as a FastAPI dependency
on authenticated routes, after JWT verification succeeds. Unauthenticated requests
(including probes and attack traffic) cannot inject trace context.

`unsafe-always`: trace context is extracted on all routes (including unauthenticated ones
such as health checks), before JWT verification. Use this when you want trace context
propagated even on auth failures. If untrusted traffic can reach your API server this can
result in data pollution or load/cost in your OTel trace store.

`never`: trace context is never extracted. Use this to disable the feature entirely.

<a id="execution_api.jwt_audience"></a>

### `jwt_audience`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | `urn:airflow.apache.org:task` |
| Type | string |
| Environment variable | `AIRFLOW__EXECUTION_API__JWT_AUDIENCE` |
| Added in | 3.0.0 |

The audience claim to use when generating and validating JWTs for the Execution API.

This variable can be a single value, or a comma-separated string, in which case the first value is the
one that will be used when generating, and the others are accepted at validation time.

Not required, but strongly encouraged

See also `config:api_auth__jwt_audience`

### `from_email`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Default | *(none)* |

| Example | `Airflow <airflow@example.com>` |
